purpose: Prove synthetic payment application, financial correction, and component-right convergence in TEST.

implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-192 E2a with immutable receipt binding, fail-closed grants, terminal convergence under suppression, and rejected and unresolved correction evidence. WELL-197 preserves P1 and E2a while evolving the Purchase constraints and isolating S1 payment consequences from P1 delivery. The migration entries for WELL-189 describe the original schema. WELL-197 MG-01 reuses E2a's acknowledged Assessment end as the original S1 claim's terminal evidence. Existing P1 and E2a effect identities remain valid.

request_flow.summary: Commerce accepts the verified canonical Account for one R399 Plan version and attempt.
Commerce qualifies evidence, locks the purchase and commits verified payment and the open obligation.
Entitlements applies the original source in its own transaction. Commerce then acknowledges the obligation.
The standalone P1 control remains R399. The signed bundle fixture freezes minor-unit lists, discounts and the resulting 5100 ZAR minor units under its own operation.
Commerce qualifies real synthetic collection identity separately from receipt identity. The first collection pays the source. A second genuine collection establishes one claim for the accepted payer.

Commerce checks exact return or component amount against the accepted snapshot and writes either unresolved or a committed consequence. Entitlements applies only its authorized change under current source and Privacy locks.

Read and compare any prior receipt binding before recording collection effects. A fresh unique receipt binds its qualified fingerprint to the genuine collection. A collision rolls back the owner transaction.

security_invariants.summary: Only a current canonical recipient session can read rights. Direct Ash grants and reads are denied.
Production excludes the producer and synthetic acceptance and application paths.
Identity checks exact owner registration and rechecks bound results. Both new owners support only empty scope.
Distinct parties are bound to the exact operation and current canonical sessions. Commerce reconciliation fails closed on either party's accepted fixture history.

Missing TEST Privacy authority fails closed. Suppression prevents creation and visibility of synthetic rights. Staff or Audit reads require a signed exact principal, source and purpose grant and return narrow projections.

An Identity block or missing TEST Privacy authority leaves the original P1 grant open. Plan creation holds a shared lock on the current eligible recipient Account through commit. Terminal TEST Privacy suppression withholds otherwise eligible grants, hides materialized rights and cannot be reset by registration.

Terminal Privacy suppression keeps existing rights hidden and prevents grants. A verified component correction still ends the exact existing right, leaving unrelated rows and monetary facts intact. The correction acknowledges an absent component without creating a row.
The existing synthetic application path refuses an attempt bound to the local WELL-218 checkout. Historical quote-less P1 retains its separate synthetic scope.

concurrency.summary: Independent payment transactions contend on the purchase row. Two concurrent delivery calls remain outstanding behind a locked consequence and converge on one source-specific right and acknowledgement.

The Commerce purchase or fixture lock serializes collection and correction. Entitlements acquires source then Privacy locks before changing rights. Acknowledgement locks the consequence in a separate transaction.

Observed PostgreSQL blockers prove receipt-key contention across accepted sources, same and fresh correction receipt replays against a held source lock, and Entitlements convergence while a first worker is blocked on the original Plan right.

idempotency_retry.summary: Replay preserves the attempt, verified payment, right and first acknowledgement time.

Direct replay binds the exact receipt fingerprint. A separate equivalent receipt resolves to the same final component or excess effect. A different accepted operation keeps its own payment and rights.

The global collection receipt key binds a SHA-256 fingerprint and its collection. Conflicting qualified observations are rejected without a new collection or claim. Another receipt for the same genuine collection returns the original application.

Known source and operation with qualified but unattributable evidence durably bind one unresolved receipt and disposition. Unresolved effects cannot be delivered or acknowledged. Invalid signatures and source or operation binding failures create neither row.

failure_recovery.summary: A connection-scoped consequence insertion cut tests Commerce rollback. Fresh BEAM scheduler runs rediscover committed open consequences through a fixture-scoped view, including after a real worker execution exhausts its configured attempt and leaves a discarded job.

Terminating the pre-commit Commerce process rolls back the uncommitted decision. Fresh BEAM workers receive only the accepted source ID, rediscover open effects, then apply and acknowledge across separate commits. The first worker encounters a real source lock. Replay after acknowledgement discovers an empty set.
A connection-scoped fault during collection receipt insert rolls back the proposed excess collection and claim. A later P1 consequence fault rolls back the receipt, collection and payment together.

A database lock timeout during ending of a suppressed right leaves the original right held and Commerce acknowledgement unset. A fresh BEAM discovers the pending source effect and ends the existing right before a separate retry acknowledges it.

tests.proves: Admission, forged input denial, independent SQL contention, a consequence-insert rollback, overlapping delivery and fresh scheduler rediscovery after missing or exhausted jobs. Separately qualified receipts preserve one P1 applied payment and a committed correction can withhold an outstanding original grant. Rejects conflicting receipt reuse across purchases, proves rollback after consequence insertion failure, and exercises missing, unavailable, and suppressed Privacy authority with observed contention. Verifies the original suppressed P1 right reaches ended before acknowledgement and the same acknowledgement is preserved on replay.
tests.limits: Synthetic only. The scheduler reads a connection-local view restricted to the owned fixture; the persisted job is executed through Oban.Testing, not by a running queue.

tests.proves: Production BEAM excludes fixture and rejects raw evidence.
Empty scope approval and replay, unknown and absent owners, stale review with committed financial provenance, legacy owner snapshot denial and fresh approval, and fresh conflict denial.

Runs the P1 and E2a migrations up, down and up in an isolated transaction-owned schema. Verifies local foreign keys, correction CHECKs and partial indexes. Verifies the global collection receipt primary key, fingerprint length check and isolated collection foreign key.
tests.limits: Uses the migration runner directly; migration ledger is not exercised.

tests.proves: Exact distinct payer, immutable allocation, partial refusal, exact rights, scoped access, independent SQL connections, killed Commerce transaction and fresh BEAM retry. Verifies cross-source receipt arbitration, exact correction and Entitlements blocking, and source-only restart after each commit boundary. Proves existing suppressed-right convergence after a failed update, sibling and independent right preservation, and unresolved versus rejected evidence for both correction effects.
tests.limits: Provider stages, runtime release, live job polling and an actual deletion journey are outside this fixture.

safe_extensions.summary: Offers, provider verification, corrections and delivery each require their approved owner contract.
Use WELL-197's shared purchase snapshot before production-shaped integration. Synthetic fixture admission deliberately has its own TEST contract.

reuse.summary: Reused Identity session authorization and AshOban rediscovery. Adapted Store patterns for immutable snapshots, SQL arbitration and exact-source grants.

Reused P1 payment uniqueness and the original commerce recovery boundary. Adapted Store Interlocks source locking, PaymentApplication uniqueness, RefundAdjustment history, Refund identities and SourceConvergence component scoping. Used Ash actions and PostgreSQL constraints. Signals and Temporal Resources are deferred because the durable scan and immutable facts cover TEST recovery and history.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: No raw business writes, provider fixture entry points, right reassignment or process-local authority.

proof_limitations: P1 uses one R399 Plan. E2a additionally uses approved TEST-only allocations and distinct verified parties. Real offers, provider cash flows, fulfilment and release remain out of scope.

Migration up/down/up uses isolated schemas and verifies foreign key targets, shape constraints and partial indexes. It does not exercise the migration ledger. The E2a rollback to P1 requires removal of TEST-only assessment and ended-right fixture rows by their owning test cleanup.
The scheduler test restricts its read to a fixture-scoped temporary view and invokes the persisted job via Oban.Testing; it does not prove live queue polling.
E2a manual recovery discovers persisted open consequences without relying on jobs. It does not certify a production scheduler for corrections or provider dispatch.
EV-012, EV-024 and EV-042 coverage is synthetic only. WELL-194 and later work retain the real provider refund, dispute and actual-stack obligations.

Receipt binding applies to newly qualified synthetic observations. Earlier disposable fixtures did not retain the receipt payload for reconstruction. The review correction introduces no historical backfill or provider-data handling.

WELL-221 keeps hosted and signed synthetic correction authority separate. The purchase payment identity is now unique for the primary collection. Excess hosted collections never create a paid benefit.
